The new library will be open to the public once the construction work is （ ） next spring.
complete 意为“完成”，construction work is completed 指工程竣工；compete“竞争”、complain“抱怨”、compile“编纂”都是形近干扰项。
Many students find it hard to （ ） to college life during their first few weeks on campus.
adjust to 意为“适应”，adjust to college life 即“适应大学生活”；adopt“采纳”，adhere to“坚持、遵守”，admit“承认”，均为形近干扰，意思不符。
The government has taken several measures to （ ） air pollution in big cities.
reduce air pollution“减少空气污染”是常用搭配；reflect“反映”、refuse“拒绝”不合语义；release“释放”意思正好相反。
Tom was so （ ） in the novel that he didn't hear his mother calling him.
be absorbed in 意为“全神贯注于”；absent from“缺席”，abandoned“被抛弃的”，attracted 后接 to/by，不与 in 搭配。
The success of the project （ ） largely on the cooperation of all team members.
depend on“取决于”；insist on“坚持”，focus on“集中于”语义不符；base 需用 be based on 的被动结构。
Please fill in this form and return it to the front desk at your earliest （ ）.
at your earliest convenience 是固定表达，意为“在您方便时尽早”；其余三词形近但意义不符。
Regular exercise can （ ） the risk of heart disease by as much as 30 percent.
lower the risk“降低风险”是常见搭配；shorten 指缩短长度或时间，weaken 指削弱力量；decline 作“下降”时为不及物动词，不能直接接宾语。
The museum's collection includes paintings, sculptures and other works of art from （ ） periods of history.
various“各种各样的”修饰 periods；variable“易变的”，valuable“贵重的”，vacant“空着的”均不合语境。
After months of hard work, she finally （ ） her goal of running a full marathon.
achieve one's goal“实现目标”是固定搭配；receive“收到”，acquire“获得（知识、技能）”，attend“参加”都不与 goal 搭配。
Online shopping has become increasingly popular because it saves time and is very （ ）.
convenient“方便的”说明网购的优点；comfortable 多指身体舒适，considerate“体贴的”用于人，constant“持续的”不合语义。
The professor asked us to （ ） our essays by Friday at the latest.
hand in“上交（作业）”；hand out“分发”，hand over“移交（权力、物品）”，hand down“传下来”。
Smartphones have had a great （ ） on the way people communicate with each other.
have an impact on“对……产生影响”；impression 多用 make an impression on“给人留下印象”，import“进口”、impulse“冲动”不合语义。
The doctor advised him to （ ） smoking, as it was seriously damaging his health.
give up smoking“戒烟”；give in“屈服”，give off“散发（气味、光）”，give out“分发；耗尽”。
Because of the heavy snow, the flight to Beijing was （ ） until the next morning.
flight was delayed“航班延误”；decline“下降、谢绝”，deny“否认”，defeat“击败”都不能修饰航班。
Volunteers play an （ ） role in helping elderly people who live alone.
play an essential role“起关键作用”；eventual“最终的”，excessive“过度的”，exclusive“独有的”均不合语境。
It is difficult to （ ） between the twins because they look exactly alike.
distinguish between A and B“区分”；extinguish“熄灭”为形近词，distribute“分配”，disturb“打扰”不合语义。
The company plans to （ ） 200 new employees to meet the growing demand for its products.
recruit employees“招聘员工”；recover“恢复”，recycle“回收利用”，recite“背诵”都是形近干扰。
Her speech was so （ ） that the whole audience stood up and applauded.
impressive“令人印象深刻的”修饰 speech；impressed 指人“感到印象深刻”，expensive“昂贵的”，extensive“广泛的”不合语义。
Students are not allowed to use their phones （ ） the exam.
during the exam“在考试期间”，during 是介词后接名词；while 是连词，需接从句；among 用于三者以上之间；within 强调“在……范围内”，不用于此处。
The price of fresh vegetables tends to （ ） with the seasons.
此处需要动词，vary with“随……而变化”；various 是形容词，variety 和 variation 是名词。
I didn't mean to hurt your feelings; I said it by （ ）.
by accident“无意中、偶然”与 didn't mean to 呼应；by chance 指“碰巧”，不强调无意；by purpose 不是正确搭配（应为 on purpose），且意思相反；incident 不与 by 搭配。
Many young people choose to （ ） their studies abroad after graduating from university.
pursue one's studies“继续深造”；persuade“说服”，pursuit 是名词，purchase“购买”均不合适。
The heavy rain caused serious （ ） to the crops in the southern provinces.
cause damage to“对……造成损害”，damage 在此为不可数名词；damages 复数意为“赔偿金”；danger“危险”不与 cause...to 搭配；injury 多指人身伤害。
She is （ ） of speaking three foreign languages fluently.
be capable of doing“有能力做”；able 用 be able to do；skillful 用 be skillful at/in；possible 不能以人为主语。
The library has a wide （ ） of books on history, science and art.
a wide range of“各种各样的、范围广泛的”；rank“等级”，rate“比率”，role“角色”均不构成该搭配。
We should （ ） full use of our spare time to improve ourselves.
make full use of“充分利用”是固定搭配，动词只能用 make。
The police are trying to find out what （ ） the fire in the warehouse last night.
cause the fire“引起火灾”，cause 可直接接宾语；result 和 lead 需要介词 in/to；made 不表示“引起”。
He failed the driving test twice, but he refused to lose （ ）.
lose heart“灰心、泄气”；lose face“丢脸”，lose one's mind/head“发疯、失去理智”，语境要求“不灰心”。
The city has introduced a new policy to （ ） people to use public transport instead of driving.
encourage sb. to do“鼓励某人做”；enable sb. to do 是“使能够”，不合语境；enhance“提高”，enforce“强制执行”不接 sb. to do。
Scientists have （ ） that the average temperature of the earth will continue to rise.
predict“预测”与 will continue to rise 相符；prevent“阻止”，pretend“假装”，prefer“更喜欢”都是形近干扰。
The two countries signed an agreement to （ ） trade and cultural exchanges.
promote trade“促进贸易”；provoke“激怒、引起”，protest“抗议”，propose“提议”，与 agreement 的目的不符。
Please keep the medicine out of the （ ） of children.
keep...out of the reach of children“放在儿童够不着的地方”是药品说明常用语；range“范围”、touch“触摸”、hold“握住”都不构成此搭配。
Despite his busy schedule, he always （ ） time to read with his daughter.
find time to do“抽出时间做”是固定搭配；look/search 后需接 for，seek time 不地道。
The manager was not satisfied with the report and asked her to （ ） it.
revise“修改”最符合“不满意要求重写”；review“复查”不一定修改，reverse“颠倒”，reveal“揭示”不合语义。
The number of people using electric cars has increased （ ） in recent years.
increase rapidly“迅速增加”；rarely“很少”，roughly“大致地”，readily“乐意地、容易地”都不修饰增长速度。
If I （ ） you, I would accept the job offer without hesitation.
与现在事实相反的虚拟条件句，if 从句用过去式，be 动词一律用 were；had been 用于与过去相反，would be 不能用在 if 从句中。
Not until he lost his job （ ） how important it was to save money.
Not until 置于句首时主句要部分倒装，即“助动词+主语+动词原形”；时间是过去，故用 did he realize；had he realized 时态不当。
The girl （ ） under the tree is my cousin.
现在分词短语 standing under the tree 作后置定语，表示主动、正在进行；stood 作定语表被动，不合语义；stands 使句子出现两个谓语。
It is high time that we （ ） measures to protect the environment.
It is high time that... 从句用虚拟语气，谓语用过去式（或 should + 动词原形），故选 took。
This is the village （ ） I spent my childhood.
先行词 village 在从句中作地点状语（spent my childhood there），用关系副词 where；which/that 需在从句中作主语或宾语。
（ ） from the top of the tower, the city looks even more beautiful.
主语 the city 与 see 是被动关系，用过去分词 Seen 作状语；Seeing 和 Having seen 表主动，To see 表目的。
By the end of next year, the new subway line （ ）.
by the end of + 将来时间，用将来完成时；subway line 与 complete 是被动关系，故用 will have been completed。
He suggested that the meeting （ ） until next week.
suggest 表“建议”时，宾语从句用 (should) + 动词原形；meeting 与 put off 是被动关系，故用 be put off。
（ ） you have any questions, please feel free to contact me.
Should 置于句首表示“万一”，是省略 if 的倒装条件句，相当于 If you should have any questions。
I would rather you （ ） the truth about the accident yesterday.
would rather 后接从句用虚拟语气，与过去事实相反用过去完成时 had told；told 表示对现在或将来的愿望。
The reason （ ） he was late was that his car broke down on the highway.
先行词 reason 后的定语从句用 why（= for which）引导；because 不能引导定语从句。
Only by working hard （ ） your dream come true.
Only + 状语置于句首时主句部分倒装，用 can you make；make sth. do 中 make 后接不带 to 的不定式。
The book, （ ） cover is torn, belongs to my roommate.
cover 与 book 是所属关系，用关系代词 whose 引导非限制性定语从句；of that 不能用于非限制性定语从句，its 不能引导从句。
She hurried to the station, only （ ） that the train had already left.
only to do 表示出乎意料的结果，意为“结果却……”；finding 表示自然的结果，与转折语气不符。
Hardly had she entered the room （ ） the phone rang.
Hardly... when... 是固定句型，意为“刚……就……”；than 与 no sooner 搭配。
The teacher, together with her students, （ ） visiting the science museum this afternoon.
together with 连接的成分不影响主语的数，谓语与 the teacher 保持一致，用单数 is；this afternoon 表将来安排，用现在进行时。
It was not until midnight （ ） the noise in the street finally stopped.
It was not until... that... 是强调句型，意为“直到……才……”，引导词只能用 that。
I regret （ ） you that your application has been rejected.
regret to do 表示“遗憾地（要）做某事”，用于告知坏消息；regret doing 表示“后悔做过某事”。
（ ） is known to all, the Great Wall is one of the wonders of the world.
As 引导非限制性定语从句，可置于句首，代指整个主句内容；Which 引导此类从句时不能置于句首，It 和 What 不符合结构。
Without your help, we （ ） the project on time last month.
without 引出含蓄虚拟条件，last month 说明与过去事实相反，主句用 could/would + have done。
随着经济的快速发展，越来越多的人选择到城市工作。
With the rapid development of the economy, more and more people choose to work in cities.
Along the rapid development of economy, more and more people choose working in cities.
As the economy rapid develops, more and more people are chosen to work in cities.
With the economy developing fast, more and more people choose to working in cities.
“随着……”译为 with the development of；choose to do 不能接 doing 或 to working；along 不表“随着”，被动语态 are chosen 意思错误。
中国是世界上历史最悠久的国家之一。
China is one of the countries with the longest history in the world.
China is one of the most longest history countries in the world.
China is the oldest history country of the world.
China is one of the country which has the longest history in the world.
one of + 最高级 + 复数名词；most longest 是双重最高级错误，one of 后需接复数 countries。
春节是中国最重要的传统节日，家人通常在除夕团聚。
The Spring Festival is the most important traditional festival in China, and families usually get together on New Year's Eve.
The Spring Festival is China's most important tradition holiday, and families usually gather in New Year's Eve.
Spring Festival is the most important festival of traditional China, families usually reunite at the New Year's Eve.
The Spring Festival is the most important traditional festival in China, which families usually meet on New Year's Eve.
“团聚”译为 get together，“在除夕”用介词 on；tradition holiday 词性错误，第三项两个分句缺连词，第四项 which 引导从句结构错误。
他直到昨天才知道考试推迟了。
He didn't know until yesterday that the exam had been postponed.
He knew until yesterday that the exam had postponed.
He didn't know that the exam was postponing until yesterday.
Until yesterday he knew that the exam has been put off.
“直到……才”用 not...until；考试“被推迟”需用被动且发生在 know 之前，用过去完成时被动 had been postponed。
保护环境是每个公民的责任。
Protecting the environment is the responsibility of every citizen.
Protect the environment is every citizen's responsibility.
To protecting environment is the duty for each citizen.
The environment protection are responsible for every citizen.
动名词短语 Protecting the environment 作主语；动词原形不能直接作主语，To protecting 结构错误，第四项主谓不一致且意思错误。
无论遇到什么困难，我们都不应该放弃。
No matter what difficulties we meet, we should not give up.
No matter what difficulties we meet, but we should not give up.
Whatever difficulties do we meet, we should not give in.
Although what difficulties we meet, we should not give up.
“无论什么”用 no matter what / whatever 引导让步状语从句，从句用陈述语序，且不能再加 but；give in 意为“屈服”，与“放弃”有差别。
This book is worth to read.
This book is worth being read.
be worth doing 以主动形式表示被动意义；worth 不接不定式，也不用 being read；deserve reading 后不能再加 it。
手机给我们的生活带来了很大的便利。
Mobile phones have brought great convenience to our lives.
Mobile phones have brought great convenient to our life.
Mobile phones bring our lives much conveniences.
Mobile phones have taken great convenience for our lives.
bring convenience to sb./sth. 为常用表达，convenience 不可数；convenient 是形容词；take...for 意思不对。
她说英语说得和英国人一样流利。
She speaks English as fluently as a native British speaker.
She speaks English as fluent as British people.
She speaks English so fluently like British.
She speaks English fluently as the same as English people.
as + 副词原级 + as，修饰动词 speaks 应用副词 fluently；so...like 和 as the same as 结构错误。
他每天花两个小时练习弹钢琴。
He spends two hours practicing the piano every day.
He spends two hours to practice the piano every day.
It takes him two hours practicing the piano every day.
He costs two hours on practicing piano every day.
spend time (in) doing sth.；spend 不接不定式；It takes sb. time to do 中应接不定式；cost 不能以人为主语。
越来越多的大学生意识到实践经验的重要性。
More and more college students have realized the importance of practical experience.
More and more college students have realized the important of practical experience.
More college students and more have realized practice experience is importance.
Many and many college students realize the practical experience's importance.
“越来越多的”用 more and more；the importance of 名词结构正确；important 是形容词，is importance 词性错误。
如果明天下雨，运动会将被推迟。
If it rains tomorrow, the sports meet will be put off.
If it will rain tomorrow, the sports meet will be put off.
If it rains tomorrow, the sports meet will put off.
If it rained tomorrow, the sports meet will be put off.
if 引导的真实条件句用一般现在时表将来（主将从现）；运动会“被推迟”应用被动语态；rained 与主句 will 时态不配合。
我们应该学会合理安排时间。
We should learn to manage our time wisely.
We should learn arranging our time reasonable.
We should learn how arrange time in reason.
We should learning to make our time reasonably.
learn to do“学会做”；manage one's time“安排时间”地道；reasonable 是形容词不能修饰动词，how arrange 缺 to，should learning 结构错误。
这次经历让我明白了团队合作的价值。
This experience made me understand the value of teamwork.
This experience made me to understand the value of teamwork.
This experience let me understanding the value of team cooperate.
This experiences made me understood the worth of teamwork.
make sb. do 中不定式省略 to；let me understanding 形式错误，cooperate 是动词；experience 表“经历”时此处单数，understood 形式错误。
尽管天气很冷，他还是坚持每天早上跑步。
Although it was very cold, he still kept running every morning.
Although it was very cold, but he still kept running every morning.
Despite it was very cold, he still kept to run every morning.
Though the weather was very cold, he still kept on to run every morning.
although 与 but 不能连用；despite 是介词，不接从句；keep doing / keep on doing 后接动名词。
他是我见过的最有耐心的老师。
He is the most patient teacher I have ever met.
He is the most patient teacher I have never met.
He is the patientest teacher that I ever met.
He is most patient teacher which I have ever met.
最高级 + 定语从句常用现在完成时 have ever met；never 意思相反；patient 的最高级是 most patient；先行词含最高级时用 that 或省略，不用 which，且最高级前要加 the。
请把灯关掉以节约用电。
Please turn off the lights to save electricity.
Please turn on the lights to save electricity.
Please turn down the lights for saving electric.
Please close off the lights to saving electricity.
turn off“关掉”，to save 表目的；turn on 意思相反，electric 是形容词，close off 意为“封闭”。
他不仅会说英语，而且会说法语。
He can speak not only English but also French.
He can speak not only English and also French.
He not can speak only English but also French.
Not only he can speak English, but also French.
not only...but also... 连接两个并列宾语；not only 置于句首时需倒装，且后半句结构要平行。
读书越多，你的知识就越丰富。
The more books you read, the richer your knowledge will be.
The more you read books, the more rich your knowledge will be.
More books you read, richer your knowledge is.
The more books you read, your knowledge will be the richer.
“越……越……”用 the + 比较级, the + 比较级；rich 的比较级是 richer；两个分句都要以 the + 比较级开头。
这家餐馆以其地道的四川菜而闻名。
This restaurant is famous for its authentic Sichuan cuisine.
This restaurant is famous as its authentic Sichuan cuisine.
This restaurant is known to its real Sichuan dishes.
This restaurant famous for its authentic Sichuan food.
be famous for“因……而著名”；be famous as 意为“作为……而著名”；be known to 意为“为……所知”；第四项缺谓语动词 is。

A. Many college students now take part-time jobs to cover their living costs.
B. Some experts worry that working too many hours can hurt students' grades.
C. Employers say that students with work experience often find jobs more easily after graduation.
D. Universities have begun to offer on-campus jobs that fit around class schedules.◆Some schools provide jobs that do not conflict with students' lessons.
D 段说大学提供与课表相配合的校内工作，即“不与上课冲突”；B 段讲的是对成绩的担忧，C 段讲毕业后就业。

A. Sleep plays a key role in helping the brain store new information.
B. Teenagers need about eight to ten hours of sleep a night, but many get far less.
C. Using phones before bed makes it harder to fall asleep because the screen light keeps the brain active.
D. Short naps in the afternoon can improve alertness without affecting night-time sleep.◆Electronic devices can interfere with falling asleep.
C 段指出睡前用手机使人难以入睡，与“电子设备干扰入睡”对应；A 段讲睡眠与记忆，D 段讲午睡的好处。

A. Plastic bags take hundreds of years to break down in the natural environment.
B. Several cities have started charging customers for each plastic bag they use at supermarkets.
C. Since the charge was introduced, the number of bags used in one city has fallen by nearly 80 percent.
D. Some shoppers complain that reusable bags are easy to forget at home.◆A policy led to a sharp drop in the use of plastic bags.
C 段给出收费后用量下降近 80% 的数据，即“大幅下降”；B 段只介绍收费政策本身，没提效果。

A. Learning a foreign language can improve a person's memory and problem-solving skills.
B. Children seem to pick up the pronunciation of a new language more easily than adults.
C. However, adults often learn grammar faster because they can understand rules more clearly.
D. Experts suggest that regular practice matters more than the age at which one starts.◆Grown-ups have an advantage in learning the rules of a language.
C 段说成年人理解规则更清楚、学语法更快，对应题干；B 段说的是儿童在发音上的优势。

A. Bike-sharing services first appeared in Chinese cities around 2016.
B. Users can find a bike with a smartphone app and leave it almost anywhere when they finish.
C. At first, too many bikes were left on sidewalks, blocking the way for pedestrians.
D. City governments later set up special parking areas and limited the number of bikes.◆Authorities took steps to solve the problem of badly parked bikes.
D 段说城市政府设置停车区并限制数量，即“采取措施解决乱停问题”；C 段只描述问题本身。

A. Volunteering gives young people the chance to learn skills that are not taught in class.
B. For example, organizing a charity event requires planning, teamwork and communication.
C. Studies show that people who volunteer regularly tend to feel happier and less stressed.
D. Many universities now count volunteer hours as part of a student's overall evaluation.◆Helping others may benefit one's mental health.
C 段指出经常做志愿者的人更快乐、压力更小，与“有益心理健康”对应；A 段讲的是技能。

A. The museum was built in 1925 and was once the home of a wealthy merchant.
B. It now holds more than 5,000 objects, including ancient coins and traditional clothing.
C. Visitors can take a free guided tour every Saturday morning at ten o'clock.
D. The museum is closed on Mondays and during the Spring Festival holiday.◆The building was originally a private house.
A 段说博物馆曾是一位富商的住宅，即“原本是私人住宅”；其他段落讲藏品、导览和闭馆时间。

A. Online courses allow students to study at their own pace and in their own time.
B. However, many learners drop out because they lack the discipline to study alone.
C. Some platforms now use study groups and deadlines to keep learners motivated.
D. Employers are gradually accepting certificates from online courses as proof of skills.◆Not all people who start online courses manage to finish them.
B 段说很多学习者因缺乏自律而中途放弃，对应“并非所有人都能完成”；C 段讲的是解决办法。

A. Coffee was first used in East Africa many centuries ago.
B. It later spread to the Middle East, where the first coffee houses opened.
C. In these coffee houses, people met to talk, listen to music and play games.
D. Today, coffee is one of the most widely traded farm products in the world.◆Coffee houses served as places for social activities.
C 段说人们在咖啡馆聊天、听音乐、玩游戏，即社交场所；B 段只提到第一批咖啡馆出现。

A. Food waste is a serious problem in many restaurants and school canteens.
B. A campaign encouraging diners to finish their meals has been launched across the country.
C. Some restaurants now offer smaller portions so that customers can order only what they need.
D. Leftover food that is still safe can be given to people in need through food banks.◆Reducing the size of dishes is one way to prevent waste.
C 段说餐馆提供小份菜，让顾客按需点餐，对应“减小分量”；D 段讲的是剩余食物的捐赠。

A. Robots are increasingly used in factories to do repetitive and dangerous work.
B. Some people fear that machines will replace millions of workers in the future.
C. Others argue that new technology will also create jobs that do not exist today.
D. To prepare for these changes, workers may need to keep learning new skills throughout their lives.◆Technology could lead to the creation of new types of employment.
C 段认为新技术会创造今天不存在的工作；B 段表达的是被取代的担忧，与题干相反。

A. Reading on paper and reading on screens can lead to different results.
B. In one study, students who read printed texts remembered the details better.
C. Researchers think that people tend to read faster and less carefully on screens.
D. Even so, digital reading is convenient and allows readers to search for information quickly.◆Screen reading has the benefit of making information easy to locate.
D 段说数字阅读方便、可快速搜索信息，对应题干；B、C 段讲的是纸质阅读的优势和屏幕阅读的缺点。

A. The city's first marathon attracted more than 20,000 runners from 30 countries.
B. The route passed through the old town, along the river and past several famous parks.
C. About 2,000 volunteers handed out water and helped runners who felt unwell.
D. Local hotels reported that almost all their rooms were fully booked that weekend.◆The event brought business to the local hotel industry.
D 段说当地酒店那个周末几乎全部订满，即带动了酒店业；A 段只讲参赛人数。

A. Many young people move to big cities after graduation in search of better jobs.
B. High rents, however, mean that a large part of their income is spent on housing.
C. As a result, some choose to share flats with friends or live farther from the city center.
D. In recent years, a growing number of graduates have returned to their hometowns to start businesses.◆Some graduates go back to where they grew up to set up their own companies.
D 段说越来越多毕业生回家乡创业，对应题干；A 段讲的是去大城市找工作，方向相反。

A. Honeybees are important because they carry pollen from one flower to another.
B. Without them, many fruits and vegetables could not be produced.
C. Unfortunately, the number of bees has dropped in many parts of the world.
D. Scientists blame chemicals used on farms, disease and the loss of wild flowers.◆Several factors have been identified as causes of the decline in bee numbers.
D 段列出化学药剂、疾病和野花减少等原因；C 段只说明蜜蜂数量下降的现象，没有讲原因。

For many years, people believed that breakfast was the most important meal of the day. Recent studies, however, have produced mixed results. Some research shows that people who skip breakfast are not necessarily heavier than those who eat it. What matters more, experts say, is the quality of the food we eat throughout the day rather than the time we eat it.◆What is the main idea of the passage?
The quality of food may be more important than when we eat it.
Breakfast is the most important meal of the day.
People who skip breakfast tend to gain weight.
Scientists have proved that breakfast is unnecessary.
末句点明主旨：专家认为全天食物的质量比进食时间更重要；B 是过去的观点，C 与原文相反，D 说法过于绝对，原文只说研究结果不一。

In the past, most people in small towns knew their neighbors well. They often helped each other with daily tasks and shared news over the fence. Today, many city residents do not even know the names of the people living next door. Busy work schedules and frequent moves are two common reasons for this change.◆According to the passage, why do many city residents not know their neighbors?
They are busy and move house often.
They do not like living in small towns.
末句指出原因是工作繁忙和频繁搬家；其余选项原文未提及。

Plants cannot move away from danger, but they are not completely helpless. When some plants are attacked by insects, they release chemicals into the air. These chemicals attract other insects that feed on the attackers. In this way, the plants use a kind of chemical message to call for help.◆What does the passage mainly discuss?
How some plants protect themselves from insects.
Why insects like to eat plants.
How plants move away from danger.
Which chemicals are harmful to plants.
全文讲植物受虫害时释放化学物质吸引天敌来自我保护；C 与第一句“植物不能移动”矛盾。

A growing number of Chinese college students are choosing to take a gap year before starting work or further study. During this year, they may travel, do volunteer work or try different jobs. Supporters believe it helps young people understand what they really want. Critics, however, worry that it may delay their careers and cost their families money.◆What is the author's attitude toward the gap year?
作者分别介绍了支持者与批评者的观点，未表明个人倾向，态度客观；indifferent 指“漠不关心”，与认真陈述不符。

The Great Green Wall is a project in Africa that aims to plant a belt of trees across the continent. It was launched in 2007 to stop the Sahara Desert from spreading south. Besides fighting the desert, the project also hopes to create jobs and improve food security for local people. Progress has been slower than planned, partly because of a lack of funding.◆Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a goal of the project?
原文提到阻止沙漠扩张、创造就业、改善粮食安全，未提吸引外国游客。

Many people think that being bored is a waste of time. But some psychologists argue that boredom can actually be useful. When we have nothing to do, our minds start to wander, and this can lead to creative ideas. Constantly checking our phones, they warn, may rob us of these valuable moments.◆According to the psychologists, what may be a negative effect of using phones all the time?
We may lose chances to think creatively.
We may become bored more easily.
末句说频繁看手机会夺走这些“宝贵时刻”，即因无聊而产生创意的机会；其他选项原文未提。

Traditional handicrafts such as paper cutting and embroidery are an important part of Chinese culture. However, as fewer young people are willing to learn these skills, some of them are in danger of disappearing. To solve this problem, several schools have added handicraft classes to their programs. Some craftsmen also sell their works online, which has helped them reach a much larger audience.◆What problem do traditional handicrafts face?
Few young people want to learn them.
They are too expensive to make.
第二句指出愿意学习的年轻人越来越少；C、D 与原文相反，B 原文未提。

Scientists have found that walking in nature can reduce stress. In one experiment, people who walked for 90 minutes in a park showed less activity in a brain area linked to negative thinking. Those who walked along a busy road showed no such change. The researchers suggest that cities should create more green spaces for their residents.◆What can be inferred from the experiment?
The environment where people walk makes a difference.
Walking along a busy road is good for the brain.
Walking for 90 minutes is too tiring for most people.
Negative thinking is caused by city life only.
在公园与在马路边步行结果不同，说明步行环境有影响；D 中 only 过于绝对。

Every year, millions of tons of clothes are thrown away. The rise of fast fashion, which offers cheap and trendy clothes, has made the problem worse. Many people buy clothes they wear only a few times. Environmental groups encourage consumers to buy fewer but better-quality items and to donate or repair old clothes.◆What do environmental groups suggest consumers do?
Buy fewer clothes of higher quality.
Buy more cheap and trendy clothes.
Throw away clothes they rarely wear.
末句说环保组织鼓励买更少但质量更好的衣服；D 中 completely 过度推断。

When Li Ming first arrived in Canada as an exchange student, he found it difficult to make friends. He was shy and worried about making mistakes in English. Then he joined the university's hiking club. Spending weekends in the mountains with other members helped him relax and speak more freely, and he soon had a group of close friends.◆What helped Li Ming make friends?
Joining a club with shared activities.
他加入徒步俱乐部，与成员一起活动后交到了朋友；其他选项原文未提。

Artificial intelligence is now used to help doctors read medical images such as X-rays. In some tests, AI systems have spotted signs of disease as accurately as experienced doctors. However, experts stress that AI should support, not replace, doctors. Human judgment is still needed to consider a patient's full medical history and to communicate with patients.◆What is the experts' view on AI in medicine?
It should be a tool that assists doctors.
It will soon replace doctors completely.
It is less accurate than young doctors.
It is too dangerous to be used in hospitals.
专家强调 AI 应辅助而非取代医生；B 与原文相反，C、D 原文未提。

The word "tea" in many languages comes from one of two Chinese pronunciations. Countries that received tea by sea, mainly through the port of Xiamen, tend to use words similar to "te". Countries that got tea over land along the Silk Road usually use words like "cha". The name of the drink therefore tells us something about how it traveled.◆Why do different languages have different words for tea?
Tea reached these countries by different routes.
Some countries grew their own tea.
Chinese people changed the name of tea.
海路传入的国家用类似 te 的词，陆路传入的用类似 cha 的词，所以差异源于传播路线。

Some parents believe that praising children for being smart helps build their confidence. But research suggests otherwise. Children praised for their intelligence often avoid difficult tasks because they are afraid of failing. In contrast, children praised for their effort are more willing to take on challenges.◆According to the research, what kind of praise is more helpful?
Praise from teachers rather than parents.
研究显示因努力受表扬的孩子更愿意接受挑战，故表扬努力更有益；C、D 原文未提。

High-speed trains have changed the way people travel in China. A trip from Beijing to Shanghai, which once took more than ten hours, now takes about four and a half. Many business travelers prefer trains to planes because stations are usually closer to city centers. Trains are also less affected by bad weather.◆Which of the following is a reason why business travelers choose trains?
Train stations are more conveniently located.
Train tickets are cheaper than plane tickets.
Trains offer better food than planes.
Trains are faster than planes on all routes.
第三句说车站通常更靠近市中心，即位置更方便；票价、餐食原文未提，D 说法绝对。

Libraries are no longer just places to borrow books. Many modern libraries offer free Wi-Fi, study rooms and even classes on computer skills. Some lend out tools, musical instruments and cameras. By providing these services, libraries remain important community centers in the digital age.◆What does the passage mainly tell us about modern libraries?
They provide a variety of services beyond lending books.
They are losing their importance in the digital age.
They charge fees for most services.
首句和后文说明现代图书馆提供多种借书以外的服务；B 与末句相反，C、D 原文未提。

Every spring, millions of birds fly thousands of kilometers to their breeding grounds. Scientists have long wondered how they find their way. Research shows that birds use several clues, including the position of the sun, the stars and the earth's magnetic field. Some species may even use their sense of smell.◆What does the word "clues" most probably mean in the passage?
Signs that help them find direction.
Dangers they face on the way.
clues 后面列举太阳、星星、地磁场，都是用于判断方向的“线索、信号”。

Some companies in Europe have tried a four-day working week without cutting workers' pay. Early results show that many employees feel less tired and more satisfied with their jobs. Surprisingly, productivity in most of these companies did not fall. Still, the model may not suit every industry, such as hospitals that need staff every day.◆What was surprising about the results?
Workers felt more tired than before.
Surprisingly 后说多数公司生产率没有下降；B、C 与原文相反，D 原文未提。

In recent years, many young Chinese people have become interested in traditional clothing known as hanfu. They wear it on holidays, to take photos at historic sites, or even in daily life. Some see it as a way to express their love for Chinese culture. The trend has also created a fast-growing market for designers and online shops.◆What is one effect of the hanfu trend mentioned in the passage?
It has made historic sites less popular.
It has caused young people to stop wearing modern clothes.
It has reduced interest in Chinese culture.
末句说这一潮流为设计师和网店创造了快速增长的市场；其余选项与原文不符。

Many people make New Year's resolutions, such as exercising more or saving money. Yet studies suggest that most people give up within a few weeks. One reason is that the goals are often too general. Experts recommend setting small, specific goals, like walking for 20 minutes three times a week, which are easier to measure and achieve.◆Why do many people fail to keep their New Year's resolutions?
Their goals are not specific enough.
They set too many small goals.
They do not have enough money.
They start too late in the year.
第三句指出原因之一是目标太笼统；专家建议设定小而具体的目标，A 正确，B 与原文相反。

Glaciers around the world are melting faster than ever before. As they shrink, sea levels rise, threatening coastal cities and islands. Glaciers also provide fresh water to hundreds of millions of people in Asia and South America. If they disappear, these communities may face serious water shortages in dry seasons.◆According to the passage, melting glaciers may cause all of the following EXCEPT ______.
原文提到海平面上升、威胁沿海、淡水短缺；未说旱季降雨增多，且与“缺水”相反。

Delivery robots have begun to appear on some university campuses in China. Students order food through an app, and a small robot brings it to their dormitory building. The robots can avoid obstacles and even call students when they arrive. Supporters say they save time, while some delivery workers worry about losing income.◆Who might be worried about the delivery robots?
末句说一些送餐员担心收入减少；学生是受益者，其余原文未提。

Laughter is good for both the body and the mind. When we laugh, our body releases chemicals that make us feel good and reduce pain. Laughing also lowers stress and may even strengthen the immune system. Interestingly, people are about 30 times more likely to laugh when they are with others than when they are alone.◆What does the last sentence suggest about laughter?
It is closely linked to social situations.
It is harmful when we are alone.
It happens only among close friends.
It is mainly a response to pain.
与他人在一起时笑的可能性是独处时的 30 倍，说明笑与社交场合密切相关；C 中 only 过于绝对。

Before the invention of the printing press, books were copied by hand, which made them rare and very expensive. Only rich people and religious institutions could afford them. Printing allowed books to be produced quickly and cheaply. As a result, more people learned to read, and new ideas spread faster than ever.◆What was the main effect of the printing press?
It made books and knowledge available to more people.
It made handwritten books more valuable.
It helped religious institutions become rich.
It made reading a hobby of the rich.
印刷术使书籍便宜易得，更多人学会阅读、新思想传播更快，即知识更普及；D 描述的是印刷术出现之前的情况。

Many cities are building "sponge cities" to deal with heavy rain. Instead of sending rainwater quickly into drains, these cities use parks, wetlands and special road surfaces to absorb and store it. The stored water can later be used to water plants or clean streets. This approach helps reduce flooding and saves water at the same time.◆What is special about a "sponge city"?
It has more drains than other cities.
It removes all wetlands and parks.
海绵城市利用公园、湿地和特殊路面吸收并储存雨水再利用；B、D 与原文相反，C 不合逻辑。

Some people believe that only young people can learn new skills well. However, a study of adults aged 58 to 86 found that those who took classes in painting, photography and a new language for three months improved their memory. The researchers concluded that learning new and challenging things keeps the brain active at any age.◆Which statement would the researchers most likely agree with?
It is never too late to learn.
Old people should avoid difficult tasks.
Only young people can learn new languages.
Painting is the best way to improve memory.
研究者认为学习新事物在任何年龄都能保持大脑活跃，即“活到老学到老”；D 把一种活动说成“最好”，属于过度推断。

Tipping customs vary greatly from country to country. In the United States, it is common to leave 15 to 20 percent of the bill for restaurant servers. In Japan, however, leaving a tip may be considered rude, because good service is seen as part of the job. Travelers are therefore advised to learn local customs before going abroad.◆What is the author's advice to travelers?
Find out about local customs in advance.
Never leave a tip in restaurants.
末句建议出国前了解当地习俗；B、C、D 都忽视了各国习俗的差异。

Each year, a large amount of electronic waste, such as old phones and computers, is produced worldwide. Only a small part of it is properly recycled. Much of the rest ends up in landfills, where harmful materials like lead can pollute soil and water. Yet e-waste also contains valuable metals such as gold and copper that could be recovered.◆What can we learn from the passage about e-waste?
It is both a danger and a possible resource.
Most of it is properly recycled.
It is worthless once thrown away.
电子垃圾既含铅等有害物质，又含金、铜等可回收金属，既是危害又是资源；B、C、D 与原文相反。

Running a marathon requires months of careful preparation. Beginners are advised to increase their weekly distance slowly, by no more than 10 percent each week. Rest days are just as important as training days, because muscles need time to recover. Many injuries happen when runners try to do too much too soon.◆What is a common cause of running injuries according to the passage?
末句说很多伤病源于过快增加训练量；文中强调休息日同样重要，B 错误。

Online reviews have a strong influence on what people buy. Many shoppers read reviews before choosing a hotel, a restaurant or a product. However, not all reviews are genuine. Some businesses pay people to write positive comments about themselves, or negative ones about competitors. Consumers should therefore read reviews with a critical eye.◆What does the phrase "with a critical eye" most probably mean?
前文说有些评论是花钱买的，因此要带着审慎、怀疑的态度阅读；critical 此处意为“批判性的”。

Pandas were once seen as a symbol of endangered animals. Thanks to decades of protection, including the creation of nature reserves and breeding programs, their numbers in the wild have risen to more than 1,800. In 2021, China changed their status from "endangered" to "vulnerable". Experts say, however, that their habitat still needs protection.◆What does the passage imply about pandas?
Protection efforts have been effective, but work must continue.
They are no longer in any danger.
Their number in the wild is decreasing.
数量上升、保护级别下调说明保护有效，但专家称栖息地仍需保护；B 忽视了最后一句，C、D 与原文相反。

Many students study by reading their notes again and again. But research shows that a more effective method is self-testing. When students try to recall information without looking at their notes, they strengthen their memory. Spreading study sessions over several days is also better than studying for long hours the night before an exam.◆Which study habit does the passage recommend?
Testing yourself and studying over several days.
Studying all night before an exam.
Looking at notes while answering questions.
文中推荐自我测试和分散学习；B、C 是被否定的方法，D 与“不看笔记回忆”相反。

Mobile payment has become a part of daily life in China. People use their phones to pay for almost everything, from meals to bus tickets. While this is convenient for most people, some elderly people who are not familiar with smartphones find it hard to keep up. Some shops have been asked to continue accepting cash for this reason.◆Why are some shops asked to continue accepting cash?
To help elderly people who cannot use mobile payment easily.
Because mobile payment is not safe.
Because cash is more convenient for young people.
To reduce the use of smartphones.
前一句说一些老人不熟悉智能手机，故要求商店继续收现金；其他选项原文未提。

The Grand Canal is the longest man-made waterway in the world, running about 1,800 kilometers from Beijing to Hangzhou. Its earliest sections were built more than 2,000 years ago. For centuries, it was used to transport grain and goods between the north and the south. In 2014, it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List.◆What was the main use of the Grand Canal in history?
Transporting goods between north and south.
第三句说几个世纪以来用于南北运输粮食和货物；其他选项原文未提。

Some scientists believe that dogs can understand human emotions. In one study, dogs were shown pictures of happy and angry human faces while listening to voices. They looked longer at the faces whose expressions matched the tone of the voices. This suggests that dogs can combine information from what they see and hear to recognize how people feel.◆What did the study find?
Dogs connect facial expressions with the tone of voices.
Dogs prefer happy faces to angry ones.
Dogs cannot recognize human faces in pictures.
Dogs only respond to their owners' voices.
狗盯着表情与语气相符的面孔看得更久，说明能把看到和听到的信息结合；B、D 原文未提，C 与原文相反。

Cities around the world are trying to reduce traffic jams. Some, like London, charge drivers a fee to enter the city center during busy hours. Others improve public transport or build bike lanes to encourage people to leave their cars at home. Each approach has its supporters and critics, and no single solution works for every city.◆What is the author's main point?
Different methods are used, and none fits all cities.
Charging drivers is the best solution.
Public transport cannot reduce traffic jams.
Bike lanes are opposed by most people.
作者介绍了多种做法，并指出没有适合所有城市的单一方案；B、C、D 均为原文未表达的片面观点。
The concert was （ ） because the singer suddenly fell ill.
cancel 意为“取消”，演出因歌手生病而取消；cancel out 是“抵消”，cancerous“癌的”，conceal“隐藏”，均不合语境。
Before signing the contract, you should read every term （ ） to avoid misunderstandings.
签合同前应“仔细地”阅读条款；carelessly“粗心地”意思相反，caringly“关爱地”、cheerfully“高兴地”与语境不符。
The new shopping mall will （ ） about 3,000 jobs for local residents.
create jobs 是固定搭配“创造就业机会”；invent 指发明新东西，discover 指发现已存在的事物，imagine“想象”，都不能与 jobs 搭配。
Our teacher always （ ） the importance of reading widely outside class.
stress 作动词意为“强调”，stress the importance of 为常见搭配；press“按压”、dress“穿衣”、distress“使苦恼”均为形近干扰。
The village is so （ ） that it takes four hours by bus to get there from the nearest town.
remote 意为“偏远的”，与坐四小时车才能到达相符；remove 是动词，recent“最近的”、regular“规律的”不合语义。
Thanks to the doctor's quick action, the patient made a full （ ） within a month.
make a full recovery 意为“完全康复”；discovery“发现”、delivery“递送”形近义异，recover 是动词，不能作 make 的宾语。
It's no use （ ） about the bad weather; let's just bring umbrellas.
complain about 意为“抱怨”，it's no use doing 表示“抱怨也没用”；explain“解释”、contain“包含”、remain“保持”都不合语境。
The professor gave a clear （ ） of how the new system works.
give a clear explanation of 意为“清楚地解释……”；expectation“期待”、exploration“探索”、expression“表达；表情”都不能说明“系统如何运作”。
Please （ ） your seat belt; the plane is about to take off.
fasten one's seat belt 是固定说法“系好安全带”；fashion“时尚”、fast“快的”、faint“昏厥；微弱的”都是形近干扰项。
Mike is very （ ）; he always keeps his promises and never tells lies.
守信、不说谎说明他“诚实”，honest 正确；humble“谦虚的”、hopeful“有希望的”与描述无关，hostile“敌对的”意思相反。
The film is （ ） on a true story that happened during the war.
be based on 意为“以……为根据”，用于电影、小说改编；rest on“依靠”、rely on“依赖”不用于此义，set 表故事背景时接 in，不说 set on a story。
Students should learn to （ ） their time between study and leisure activities.
balance ... between ... 意为“在……之间平衡”；balloon“气球；膨胀”、bounce“弹跳”、ballot“投票”都是形近干扰项。
Although the two cities are far apart, they have a lot in （ ）.
have a lot in common 是固定搭配“有很多共同之处”；in general“总体上”、in public“公开地”、in total“总共”都不表示共同点。
The museum does not （ ） visitors to take photos of the paintings.

C. They also give city residents a place to grow vegetables and relax.
D. However, older buildings may need to be made stronger before a garden can be added.◆Green roofs can help save energy during hot weather.
B 段说屋顶植物让建筑在夏天更凉爽，减少空调使用，即节能；C 段讲种菜休闲，D 段讲旧楼需要加固。

A. Many elderly people in China have started learning to use smartphones.
B. Some universities for senior citizens offer free courses on mobile apps.
C. Grandchildren are often the most patient teachers for their grandparents.
D. Learning these skills allows older people to video chat with family and order taxis by themselves.◆Younger family members are often good at helping older people learn.
C 段说孙辈往往是祖父母最有耐心的老师；B 段讲老年大学课程，D 段讲学会后的好处。

A. Wild elephants in Yunnan made headlines in 2021 when a group walked hundreds of kilometers north.
B. Scientists are still not sure why the elephants left their home in the forest.
C. Local people were told to stay indoors and to leave food out to keep the animals away from towns.
D. The journey drew public attention to the need to protect elephant habitats.◆The reason for the animals' long journey remains unclear.
B 段说科学家仍不确定大象为何离开森林，即原因不明；A 段讲事件本身，D 段讲事件带来的关注。

A. The city of Weifang in Shandong is known as the world's kite capital.
B. Its kite-making history goes back more than 2,000 years.
C. Every April, an international kite festival attracts flyers from dozens of countries.
D. Local craftsmen are now teaching kite-making in schools to keep the skill alive.◆Efforts are being made to pass a traditional skill on to young people.
D 段说手艺人在学校教做风筝以保持这门手艺，即传承给年轻人；B 段讲历史，C 段讲风筝节。

A. Second-hand trading apps let people sell things they no longer need.
B. Students often use them to buy used textbooks at low prices.
C. Buying used goods also reduces waste and saves natural resources.
D. Users are warned, however, to check items carefully because some sellers give false descriptions.◆Buyers should be careful because not all information about products is true.
D 段提醒用户仔细检查物品，因为有卖家虚假描述；B 段讲学生买旧书，C 段讲环保。

A. Fitness apps that count steps and record heart rates are now very popular.
B. Some users say that setting daily goals encourages them to move more.
C. Doctors note that the data from these apps is not always accurate.
D. Experts suggest using the apps as a guide rather than relying on them completely.◆The numbers shown by these apps can sometimes be wrong.
C 段说医生指出这些应用的数据不总是准确；B 段讲设定目标的激励作用，D 段讲专家建议的使用方式。

A. Short-video platforms have become a major source of entertainment for young people.
B. Some videos teach useful skills such as cooking or basic home repairs.
C. Spending too much time watching short clips may make it harder to focus on long tasks.
D. Some platforms now remind users to take a break after a certain amount of viewing time.◆These platforms are now one of the main ways young people have fun.
A 段说短视频平台已成为年轻人主要的娱乐来源；B 段讲学技能，D 段讲平台的休息提醒。

A. Schools in many parts of China hold earthquake drills at least once a term.
B. During the drills, students practice hiding under their desks and leaving the building in order.
C. Teachers time the process to see how quickly everyone can reach the playground.
D. Experts say regular practice helps people stay calm in a real emergency.◆Students regularly practice what to do if the ground starts shaking.
A 段说学校每学期至少举行一次地震演练，即定期练习；B 段讲演练的具体动作，D 段讲练习的好处。

A. Dumplings have been eaten in China for more than 1,800 years.
B. In northern China, families often make dumplings together on Spring Festival Eve.
C. Their shape is similar to that of ancient Chinese money, so they are thought to bring wealth.
D. Today, frozen dumplings are sold in supermarkets around the world.◆People believe this food brings good fortune because of how it looks.
C 段说饺子形状像古代钱币，被认为能带来财富；B 段讲除夕包饺子的习俗，D 段讲超市售卖。

A. China launched its Tianwen-1 mission to Mars in July 2020.
B. The spacecraft traveled for about seven months before reaching the planet.
C. Its rover, Zhurong, studied the soil and rocks on the surface for about a year.
D. The information collected will help scientists understand whether Mars once had water.◆The data gathered may answer questions about the planet's past.
D 段说收集的信息有助于了解火星过去是否有水；B 段讲飞行时间，C 段讲火星车的考察活动。

A. Listening to music while studying is a habit for many students.
B. Some studies show that music without words can help people concentrate.
C. Songs with lyrics, however, may distract readers because the brain tries to process the words.
D. The best choice may depend on the person and the type of task.◆Music containing words may make it harder to read.
C 段说带歌词的歌曲会分散阅读者注意力；B 段说无歌词音乐有助于专注，与陈述相反。

A. Many cities have set up public charging stations for electric cars.
B. Drivers can find the nearest station and check if it is free through a mobile app.
C. Charging a car still takes much longer than filling a tank with petrol.
D. Engineers are developing faster batteries to solve this problem.◆An app can show drivers whether a charging point is available.
B 段说司机可通过手机应用找到最近的充电站并查看是否空闲；A 段只说建了充电站，D 段讲电池研发。

A. Bookstores in China have changed a lot over the past ten years.
B. Many of them now include cafés, art spaces and areas for public talks.
C. Owners say these changes help attract customers who usually buy books online.
D. Some bookstores stay open 24 hours, offering a quiet place to read at night.◆Book shops look very different today compared with a decade ago.
A 段说过去十年书店变化很大，与陈述对应；B 段讲具体的新设施，D 段讲 24 小时营业。

A. Many people feel nervous when they have to speak in front of a group.
B. Preparing well and practicing in front of friends can reduce this fear.
C. Some speakers find it helpful to focus on one friendly face in the audience.
D. With experience, most people become more relaxed on stage.◆Rehearsing with people you know may make you less anxious.
B 段说充分准备并在朋友面前练习可以减少恐惧；C 段讲关注观众中友善的面孔，D 段讲经验的作用。

Although about 70 percent of the earth's surface is covered by water, only a tiny part of it can be used by humans. Most of the water is salty, and much of the fresh water is frozen in ice. As populations grow, many regions are facing serious water shortages. Experts suggest that saving water at home, such as fixing leaking pipes, can make a real difference.◆Why is usable water limited according to the passage?
Most water is either salty or frozen.
The earth's surface has little water.
Leaking pipes waste most fresh water.
Water is too expensive to clean.
第二句说明大部分水是咸水，淡水又多冻结在冰中；B 与“70% 被水覆盖”矛盾，C、D 原文没有这样说。

Fewer people today write letters by hand. Most of us type on keyboards or phones instead. Some researchers, however, have found that students who take notes by hand remember lecture content better than those who type. They believe that writing by hand forces people to think about and summarize the information, rather than copying every word.◆Why do handwritten notes help memory, according to the researchers?
People have to process and summarize information.
Students can copy every word the teacher says.
Paper notebooks are easier to carry.
末句指出手写迫使人们思考并概括信息；B、D 原文未提，C 是打字者的做法，正是研究者认为效果差的原因。

Noise is not just annoying; it can also harm our health. Long-term exposure to traffic noise has been linked to poor sleep, high blood pressure and even heart disease. The World Health Organization recommends that night-time noise outside homes should be kept below 40 decibels. Some cities have begun planting trees and building sound barriers along busy roads.◆What is the passage mainly about?
The health effects of noise and ways to reduce it.
Why trees grow better along busy roads.
How the WHO measures air quality.
The causes of heart disease in cities.
全文先讲噪音危害健康，再讲城市的降噪措施；B 曲解种树的目的，C 偷换为空气质量，D 只是细节且范围不符。

Sitting for long hours has become a normal part of modern life. Office workers, drivers and students may sit for more than ten hours a day. Studies show that this can increase the risk of weight gain and back pain, even for people who exercise regularly. Doctors recommend standing up and moving around for a few minutes every half hour.◆What can we learn about people who exercise regularly?
They may still be harmed by sitting too long.
They are not affected by long hours of sitting.
They usually sit for less than ten hours a day.
They seldom suffer from back pain.
第三句说即使定期锻炼的人，久坐也会增加风险；B、D 与原文相反，C 原文未提。

The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes linking China with Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe. Along these routes, merchants carried silk, tea and porcelain westward and brought back horses, glass and spices. Ideas, religions and inventions such as papermaking also spread along the way.◆What does the passage say about the Silk Road?
It allowed both goods and ideas to be exchanged.
It was one long road built by China.
Only silk was traded along it.
It connected China mainly with Africa.
原文说商品双向流通，思想、宗教和发明也随之传播；B 与第一句矛盾，C 以偏概全，D 原文未提非洲。

On hot summer days, city centers are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside. This is because concrete and roads absorb heat during the day and release it at night. Trees can help cool cities by providing shade and releasing water through their leaves. A study in one city found that streets with many trees were up to 5°C cooler than streets without them.◆According to the passage, how do trees cool down cities?
By giving shade and releasing water.
By absorbing heat from roads at night.
By blocking wind from the countryside.
By reducing the number of cars.
第三句明确说树木通过遮阴和叶子释放水分降温；B 是混凝土的特点，C、D 原文未提。

Teaching others is one of the best ways to learn. When students know they will have to explain something to classmates, they tend to organize the information more clearly in their minds. Explaining also helps them find gaps in their own understanding. That is why some teachers ask students to work in pairs and take turns teaching each other.◆Why do some teachers ask students to teach each other?
Explaining helps students understand material better.
Teachers want to reduce their own workload.
It is the fastest way to finish a lesson.
前文说明讲解能帮助学生理清思路、发现不足，末句 That is why 指出原因；B、C、D 都是原文没有的推测。

Can colors affect our mood? Many designers believe so. Blue is often used in offices and bedrooms because it is thought to make people feel calm. Red, on the other hand, is linked with energy and excitement, which is why it often appears in fast-food restaurants. However, scientists point out that people's reactions to colors also depend on culture and personal experience.◆What do scientists think about the effects of colors?
They vary from person to person and culture to culture.
They are exactly the same for everyone.
They have been proved to be unimportant.
末句说人们对颜色的反应还取决于文化和个人经历；B 与之相反，C、D 原文没有这样说。

The Hani Rice Terraces in Yunnan cover the slopes of mountains like giant staircases. They were built by the Hani people over 1,300 years ago. A clever system carries water from the forests at the top of the mountains down through each terrace. In 2013, the terraces were listed as a World Heritage Site, and they now attract many photographers.◆Where does the water for the terraces come from?
Forests at the top of the mountains.
Rivers at the foot of the mountains.
第三句说水从山顶森林引下流经各层梯田；其余选项原文均未提及。

Microplastics are pieces of plastic smaller than five millimeters. They come from broken-down bottles and bags, as well as from synthetic clothes when they are washed. Scientists have found microplastics in oceans, soil and even drinking water. Although their effects on human health are not yet fully understood, many researchers believe it is wise to reduce plastic use now.◆What is the researchers' attitude toward microplastics?
虽然健康影响尚不清楚，研究者仍认为应现在就减少塑料使用，是“谨慎”的态度；indifferent“漠不关心”、optimistic“乐观”、amused“觉得好笑”都不符合。

Many people believe they can do several things at once, such as texting while listening to a lecture. In fact, the brain does not really multitask. It switches quickly between tasks, and each switch costs time and attention. Studies show that people who often multitask make more mistakes and take longer to finish their work.◆What does the passage suggest about multitasking?
It lowers the quality and speed of work.
It is a skill everyone should learn.
It helps the brain work faster.
It is only a problem for students.
末句说经常一心多用的人错误更多、耗时更长；B、C 与原文相反，D 原文未限定于学生。

Smart home devices, such as voice assistants and security cameras, make daily life more convenient. You can turn on the lights or check who is at the door with your phone. However, these devices also collect a large amount of personal data. Experts advise users to change default passwords and to read privacy settings carefully.◆What is the experts' advice?
Protect personal information when using the devices.
Stop using smart home devices completely.
Buy only the most expensive devices.
Let the company manage your passwords.
专家建议修改默认密码、仔细查看隐私设置，即保护个人信息；B、C 原文未提，D 与建议相反。

Humpback whales are famous for their songs. Only male whales sing, and each song can last up to 20 minutes. Interestingly, all the males in one area sing nearly the same song, which slowly changes over the years. Scientists think the songs may be used to attract females, but they are still studying exactly why the whales sing.◆What do we know about the whales' songs?
Males in the same area share a similar song.
Both male and female whales sing.
第三句说同一区域的雄鲸唱几乎相同的歌；B 与“只有雄鲸唱歌”矛盾，C 与“逐渐变化”矛盾，D 与末句“仍在研究”矛盾。

Writing down three good things that happen each day may make you happier. In one study, people who kept such a "gratitude journal" for a week reported feeling happier for up to six months. Researchers explain that the habit trains people to notice positive events they might otherwise ignore.◆Why does keeping a gratitude journal work?
It helps people pay attention to good things.
It makes people forget bad experiences.
It encourages people to make more friends.
末句说这个习惯训练人们注意到可能被忽视的积极事件；B、C、D 原文未提。

China has hundreds of local dialects, some of which are so different that speakers cannot understand each other. As more young people use Mandarin at school and at work, some dialects are spoken mainly by older people. To save them, some researchers are recording elderly speakers, and a few schools have added dialect songs and stories to their lessons.◆Why are some dialects in danger?
Young people mostly speak Mandarin instead.
Old people refuse to use them.
They are too difficult to record.
第二句说年轻人在学校和工作中多用普通话，方言主要由老人使用；B、C 与原文相反，D 原文未提。

Cooking at home has many benefits. Meals made at home usually contain less salt, sugar and oil than restaurant food. Cooking can also save money and bring family members together. Yet many young workers say they are too busy to cook. Some have found a solution: preparing several meals at the weekend and storing them in the fridge for the week.◆How do some busy young workers solve their problem?
By cooking meals in advance at weekends.
By eating at restaurants every day.
By asking their parents to cook for them.
末句说他们周末准备好几餐存进冰箱；B、C、D 原文都未提及。

Some companies now use 3D printers to build small houses. A large machine squeezes out layers of special concrete, following a computer design. A basic house can be printed in less than two days and at a lower cost than traditional building methods. Supporters believe the technology could help provide homes quickly after natural disasters.◆What advantage of 3D-printed houses is mentioned?
They can be built quickly and cheaply.
They are larger than ordinary houses.
They do not need any concrete.
They can survive any natural disaster.
第三句说房子两天内可打印完成且成本更低；B 原文说是 small houses，C 与“特殊混凝土”矛盾，D 曲解了“灾后快速提供住房”。

In a job interview, what you say is important, but so is how you say it. Interviewers often notice body language, such as eye contact, posture and handshakes. Candidates who sit up straight and look at the interviewer tend to appear more confident. On the other hand, crossing your arms may make you seem unfriendly.◆What does the word "posture" in the passage most probably mean?
The way a person sits or stands.
The tone of a person's voice.
The speed at which a person talks.
posture 与 eye contact、handshakes 并列为肢体语言，下文 sit up straight 是其例子，故指“坐姿或站姿”；B、C、D 都不属于原文所举的肢体语言。

Ants are tiny, but together they can do amazing things. Some species build nests that contain millions of individuals. When they find food, ants leave a chemical trail so that others can follow it. Some ants even link their bodies to form bridges across gaps. No single ant is in charge; the colony works well because each ant follows simple rules.◆What makes an ant colony work well?
A leader gives orders to all ants.
Each ant can find food on its own.
末句说没有任何一只蚂蚁负责，蚁群运转良好是因为每只蚂蚁遵守简单规则；B 与 No single ant is in charge 矛盾，C、D 不是原因。

Wheelchair users often face problems in cities, such as steps without ramps and buses they cannot get on. In recent years, many Chinese cities have added lifts to subway stations and lowered the floors of buses. These changes help not only disabled people, but also elderly people and parents with baby strollers.◆Who benefits from the changes mentioned in the passage?
Several groups of people, including the elderly.
末句说这些改变不仅帮助残障人士，也帮助老人和推婴儿车的父母；B 与 not only ... but also 矛盾，C、D 原文未提。

In some remote mountain areas, delivering medicine used to take hours on rough roads. Now drones can carry medical supplies to village clinics in about twenty minutes. The drones are especially useful in emergencies, such as when a patient urgently needs blood. However, bad weather can still stop them from flying.◆What limitation of the drones is mentioned?
They cannot fly in bad weather.
They are too expensive for villages.
末句指出恶劣天气仍可能使无人机无法飞行；B 与“二十分钟送达”矛盾，C 以偏概全，D 原文未提。

Octopuses are among the most intelligent animals in the sea. In laboratories, they have learned to open jars to get food inside. Some have even escaped from their tanks at night and returned before morning. Unlike humans, an octopus has most of its nerve cells in its arms, which allows each arm to act partly on its own.◆Which of the following is true about octopuses?
Their arms can act partly independently.
Most of their nerve cells are in their heads.
They cannot be studied in laboratories.
末句说章鱼大部分神经细胞在腕足中，使每条腕能部分独立行动；B 与原文相反，C、D 与实验室中的例子矛盾。

A short nap in the afternoon can improve alertness and mood. Experts say the best nap lasts about 20 minutes. If you sleep longer, you may enter deep sleep and feel groggy when you wake up. Naps should also be taken before 3 p.m., as late naps can make it harder to fall asleep at night.◆Why should naps not be too long?
People may feel tired and confused after waking.
Long naps improve mood too much.
Long naps are only for children.
原文说睡太久会进入深睡眠，醒来后昏昏沉沉（groggy）；B、C、D 原文均未提及。

Food companies spend huge amounts of money on advertisements aimed at children. Many of these ads promote snacks and drinks that are high in sugar. Because young children cannot easily tell the difference between ads and normal programs, some countries have banned such advertising during children's TV shows.◆Why have some countries banned certain ads?
Young children cannot easily recognize ads.
The ads are too expensive to make.
Children do not watch TV any more.
Food companies asked for the ban.
末句说幼儿难以区分广告和普通节目，所以一些国家禁止此类广告；B、C、D 原文未提。

Before paper was invented, the Chinese wrote on bamboo strips and silk. Bamboo was heavy, and silk was expensive. Around 105 AD, Cai Lun improved the method of making paper from tree bark, old cloth and fishing nets. His paper was light and cheap, and it soon became widely used. Papermaking later spread to the Arab world and Europe.◆What was the main advantage of Cai Lun's paper?
It was made only from bamboo.
It was used only by emperors.
原文说蔡伦的纸又轻又便宜，因此很快得到广泛使用；B 原文未比较，C 与原料描述矛盾，D 与 widely used 矛盾。

In many big cities, young people find it hard to buy a home because prices are so high. More of them are choosing to rent instead. Renting gives them freedom to move when they change jobs. However, some worry that renters have less security, as landlords can raise the rent or ask them to leave.◆What is one disadvantage of renting mentioned in the passage?
Renters may be asked to move out.
Renting costs more than buying a home.
Renting is only possible in big cities.
末句说房东可能涨租或要求租客搬走，安全感较低；B 原文未提，C 与“换工作时可自由搬家”矛盾，D 原文未提。

Deserts receive strong sunshine almost every day, which makes them ideal places for solar power. China has built huge solar farms in deserts in Qinghai and Inner Mongolia. Interestingly, the solar panels provide shade, which reduces water loss from the ground and allows some plants to grow underneath them. Local farmers have even let sheep graze there.◆What unexpected effect do the solar panels have?
They help plants grow by shading the ground.
They attract more rain to the area.
原文用 Interestingly 引出：太阳能板提供遮阴，减少水分流失，使植物能生长；B、C 原文未提，D 与农民放羊矛盾。

The number of children with short sight has risen sharply in East Asia. Many people blame screens, but researchers have found another important factor: time spent outdoors. Children who spend at least two hours a day outside are less likely to become short-sighted, possibly because bright daylight helps the eyes develop normally.◆What does the research suggest parents should do?
Let children spend more time outdoors.
Keep children indoors on sunny days.
研究发现每天户外两小时以上的孩子更不易近视，故应让孩子多去户外；B 过于绝对，C 与研究相反，D 原文未提。

Some university students have set up book exchange corners in their dormitories. Students leave books they have finished and take others they want to read. There are no fees and no deadlines. The organizers say the project not only saves money but also helps students discover books they would never have chosen themselves.◆What is one benefit of the book exchange corners?
Students find books they might not have chosen.
Students can earn money by selling books.
Students must return books within a week.
Students get help with their homework.
末句说该活动帮助学生发现自己原本不会选的书；B 与 no fees 不符，C 与 no deadlines 矛盾，D 原文未提。

False information spreads quickly online, sometimes faster than the truth. A story that makes people angry or surprised is more likely to be shared. Before sharing a news story, experts suggest checking where it comes from and whether other reliable sources report the same thing.◆Why does false information often spread quickly?
It is always shorter than real news.
It is shared only by young people.
第二句说令人愤怒或惊讶的消息更容易被转发，即引发强烈情绪；B、C、D 原文都未提及。

The murals in the Mogao Caves of Dunhuang have survived for more than 1,000 years. But sand, humidity and the breath of visitors are slowly damaging them. To protect the paintings, experts have created high-quality digital copies. People can now explore the caves online, and the number of visitors allowed inside each day is limited.◆What is the purpose of making digital copies?
To protect the murals while allowing people to see them.
To replace the real caves completely.
To attract more visitors into the caves.
To sell the paintings to collectors.
数字化既保护壁画（同时限制进洞人数），又让人们在网上参观；B 过于绝对，C 与限流相反，D 原文未提。

Some famous tourist spots are suffering from too many visitors. In cities like Venice, crowds fill narrow streets and housing prices have risen, pushing local residents out. Some places now charge entry fees or limit the number of tourists. Travel experts encourage people to visit less popular destinations or to travel outside peak seasons.◆What do travel experts suggest?
Visiting places that are less crowded.
末句说专家鼓励人们去不太热门的地方或在淡季出游；C 与原文相反，B、D 原文未提。

Several countries have introduced a tax on sugary drinks. The aim is to encourage companies to reduce sugar and people to choose healthier drinks. In the UK, many drink makers lowered the sugar in their products before the tax even started. Critics, however, argue that the tax hurts poorer families most.◆What happened in the UK?
Companies reduced sugar before the tax began.
第三句说许多饮料商在征税开始前就降低了含糖量；B、C 原文未提，D 与批评者“对穷人伤害最大”的说法相反。

Many people think chess is just a game, but it can also be good for the brain. Playing chess requires planning several moves ahead and imagining the opponent's response. Some schools have added chess to their after-school programs, hoping it will improve students' concentration and problem-solving skills.◆Why have some schools introduced chess?
To develop students' focus and thinking skills.
To train students for professional competitions.
